title: Compact interview loop and onboarding micro-sprint
content:
Purpose:
A lean, repeatable interview loop and a complementary 30-day micro-onboarding plan targeted at IC hires (IC-2 to IC-4) and early managers. Goal: reduce time-to-offer, standardize decision quality, and accelerate first-month impact.

Scope / When to use this template:
- Roles: SWE (platform/infra), ML infra, SRE, Developer Experience, Product (PM PM-i). Avoid for executive hires — use executive kit.
- Use when hiring velocity needs to increase but we must preserve quality gates and candidate experience.

High-level principles (why this is different):
- Timeboxed, compact: max 5 interview touchpoints, one technical take-home permitted only for complex system roles.
- Clear weights and pass thresholds so hiring managers and interviewers make consistent calls.
- Candidate experience first: every candidate gets a scheduling window <72h from screen to loop, offer decision within 5 business days.
- Onboarding micro-sprint: first 30 days focused on 3 outcome-oriented milestones rather than checklists of items.

Interview loop template (recommended):
1) Recruiter screen (30 min) — scheduling + salary band check, career motivations, basic fit flags. (Owner: Recruiter)
2) Hiring manager resume review + role clarity (30 min asynchronous/meeting) — manager confirms target competencies and must-know constraints.
3) Technical design/system loop (60 min) — pair/whiteboard focusing on architecture tradeoffs and scaling. (Owner: Senior Eng)
4) Deep dive or paired coding (45-60 min) — live exercise or take-home review (if previously assigned). For ML infra roles, include model-serving/latency tradeoffs.
5) Behavioral + collaboration fit (45 min) — cross-functional partner or future teammate. Scenario-based, conflict resolution, communication.
6) Hiring manager debrief (15–30 min) — decision alignment and calibration.

Notes:
- Keep total interview time <= 4 hours across rounds. Interviewers must submit written score + 2-sentence rationale within 24 hours.
- If candidate fails on a single critical must-have (security, legal eligibility, severe gap), recruiter flags for immediate no-hire.

Scoring rubric (single-sheet numeric):
- Tech fundamentals (30%) — algorithms/systems thinking, correctness when relevant. Score 1–5.
- Design & scale (25%) — tradeoffs, latency/cost considerations, KV/serving strategies. Score 1–5.
- Problem-solving & learning (15%) — ability to scaffold, ask clarifying Qs, learn on the fly. Score 1–5.
- Collaboration & communication (20%) — clarity, async docs, conflict handling. Score 1–5.
- Culture & ownership signals (10%) — bias for action, reliability evidence. Score 1–5.

Composite score calculation: weighted sum, normalized to 100. Thresholds: >=70 recommend hire, 55–69 hold/second look (small targeted loop), <55 no-hire. Hiring manager can override with documented rationale (must be added to candidate file).

Decision matrix (practical):
- Strong hire: Composite >=80 + unanimous behavioral/tech signals. Move to offer, send comp packet within 48h.
- Hire: Composite 70–79 or manager strong recommendation after debrief. Draft offer and loop finance/comp.
- Hold: 55–69: schedule 1 focused follow-up (45 min) on missing area (e.g., system design or collaboration). Limit: one follow-up only.
- No-hire: <55 or critical fail. Provide short, actionable feedback.

Candidate experience checklist (recruiter owner):
- Before loop: send role summary, interviewers' names + LinkedIn, format expectations, and a 48h calendar window.
- During loop: interviewer intros (1 line each), timekeeper present, one person in loop flagged as candidate advocate for any issues.
- After loop: decision timeline communicated within 24h of the hiring manager debrief; decision communicated no later than 5 business days from last interview.
- Feedback: Offer or no-hire feedback includes 2–3 concrete examples.

Operational SLAs & targets (recruiting metrics):
- Time from screen to loop start: target <=72h.
- Time from final interview to decision: target <=5 business days.
- Offer acceptance target: 70% for IC-2/3; measure variance by role family.
- Interviewer completion rate: >95% submit rubric within 24h.

Onboarding micro-sprint (first 30 days):
Objectives: 3 measurable outcomes (pick + name them in offer onboarding doc). Examples:
  A) Merge first infra bugfix / PR with CI green and peer approvals.
  B) Document (public) one serving-performance regression test and runbook.
  C) Owner on a clearly scoped feature/bug to deliver by day 30.

Week 0 (pre-start, recruiter/IT):
- Laptop order + env access requests submitted (KMS, VPN, internal GDrive)
- First-week schedule sent (buddy + manager 1:1s, team intro, orientation).

Week 1 (setup + context):
- Day 1: orientation, benefits, security brief, account provisioning check.
- Day 2–3: shadow pair on infra runbooks, read core docs (serving runtime primer, infra diagram).
- Day 4–5: small starter task (bug/triage) and PR; manager sets 30-day outcomes.

Week 2 (deliver small win):
- Focus: complete starter PR, add to onboarding doc, get peer review.
- 1:1 weekly sync: unblock list review, training gaps, escalation path.

Week 3–4 (ownership ramp):
- Start work on outcome B or C; include design doc draft for manager review.
- Run required security checklist for any infra access used.
- End-of-30-day: demo 30-day outcomes in team demo slot + short retro with manager.

Onboarding success signals (manager):
- Candidate shipped a production PR or a validated experiment.
- Documented runbook/component knowledge shared with team.
- Self-reported confidence 3/5 or higher on core responsibilities and clear plan for next 60 days.

Operational notes for People Ops & Hiring Managers:
- Interviewer training: 45-min calibration session quarterly; include anonymized score normalization examples.
- Score normalization: every 6 weeks, recruiting ops runs a calibration report against hires vs. downstream performance (SLO: reduce false-positives).
- Diversity & fairness check: mandatory panel review for final on-site offers for IC-3+.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Should we allow a distributed 2x15min interview (split-tech) instead of one 60-min design for calendar flexibility? Pros/cons to capture. (JIRA-REC-4821)
- Where to store final 30-day outcomes as canonical? Confluence or HRIS? Add to new-hire profile in HRIS.
- Update template to include remote timezone expectations explicitly.

Appendix (examples & snippets):
- Sample 2-sentence actionable feedback for no-hire: "Thanks for interviewing — we decided not to move forward due to gaps in distributed system tradeoffs for the role. Suggest preparing: design patterns for sharded KV caches and read/ write amplification tradeoffs."
- Quick interviewer prompt bank (useful phrases): "Talk me through an outage you owned"; "What metrics would you pick to evaluate a cache strategy?"; "How do you prioritize latency vs. cost in a multi-tenant runtime?"

Last edited notes: draft and tested in small pilot with Platform infra hiring in Oct 2025. Collabs: Marco (recruiting data), Jamal (hiring manager playbook), Leah (onboarding ops). Planning to present to People Ops leadership on 2026-02-20.

(Sign-off) Aisha Patel — people-ops lead (draft).
